item.title: Russia-linked priests preaching Azerbaijan war, Armenia warns EU
item.description: “One of the archbishops in Armenia had started a movement to [reactivate] ... the [Nagorno-Karabakh] conflict”, warned Armenian prime minister Nikol Pashinyan.

item.title: MEPs vote to change controversial ‘chat scanning’ measures
item.description: As the clock is running out on the current rules, MEP vote for substantive changes to the controversial chat-scanning measures while agreeing to extend the temporary rules for fighting child sexual abuse material online.

item.title: What Sarkozy’s corruption appeal means for cleaning up European politics
item.description: It is easy to treat the case as just a French affair. In reality, the appeal carries wider international stakes and has become a stress test for the rule-of-law ecosystem under pressure across the EU.

item.title: Listen: Is the alliance between right and far-right parties the new norm in Europe?
item.description: The European Parliament’s centre-right is increasingly voting with far-right parties — first on migration, now on deregulation. As similar alliances emerge in national governments across Europe, the long-standing political “cordon sanitaire” against the far right is weakening, raising questions about whether this shift could soon become the new norm.

item.title: Russian fossil-fuel daily revenues up 14% since start of US-Israel attack on Iran
item.description: Russia has earned an estimated €6bn in fossil-fuel, or €510m per day, since the attacks on Iran, according to a new analysis published on Thursday.

item.title: Ukraine Battlefield update (Day 1,477): ‘I don’t want to any more, but I still have to’ – what I heard from a Ukrainian soldier
item.description: Ukrainian anti-tank ditches contain barbed wire, between them rows of dragon’s teeth connected by steel cables, and between those further belts of barbed wire. Parts of the ditches were flooded by melted snow.

item.title: 31 days to election: Orbán claims Ukrainians are threatening his children and grandchildren
item.description: In our regular digest of the week’s news from the Hungarian campaign trail: latest opinion polls, a Hungarian delegation to Ukraine to inspect the damaged Russian oil pipeline, claims Kremlin-approved Russian disinfo is amplifying Fidesz campaign messaging, Hollywood star Mark Ruffalo calls on Hungarians to free themselves from Orban, and physical attacks on independent journalists.

item.title: EU governments face ‘no immediate concerns’ on oil supply amid record emergency release
item.description: The EU's bodies on oil and gas supply held meetings on Thursday morning following the International Energy Agency's decision to open access to 400m barrels of reserves.

item.title: How the EU lets plastic be labelled ‘recycled’ at just 2.5% re-used content
item.description: Plastic products in the EU could soon be labelled "recycled" — even when they contain barely any recycled material. A new definition backed by most member states allows plastics with as little as 2.5 percent waste-derived content. Critics warn that the rule relies on accounting tricks that may mask fossil-based plastic production.

item.title: EU-made facial recognition ended up scanning schoolchildren in Brazil
item.description: The EU restricts biometric surveillance at home – but its landmark AI Act does nothing to prevent European companies from exporting the same technology abroad.
